title: K-flat preservation and quasi-isomorphism inversion after point evaluation
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme whose category of module sheaves [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] admits a derived category. Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and let $p:X\to (\mathrm{pt},A)$ be the global sections ringed-space morphism [def-pc-global-derived-rhom]. Let $e:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{pt}})\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ be an equivalence whose forward functor is naturally isomorphic to evaluation. Let $P:\operatorname{Mod}(A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ be additive, strong monoidal, and a left adjoint. Assume its object and morphism formulas are exactly inverse evaluation followed by inverse image and change of rings along the adjoint structure map of $p$ [lem-pc-kflat-pullback-preservation]. Then its termwise homotopy functor $P^h$ sends every K-flat object [def-pc-kflat-complex] to a K-flat object. Moreover, for a quasi-isomorphism $a:K\to M$ between K-flat homotopy objects, $Q_X^h(P^h(a))$ is an isomorphism. No flatness or boundedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Cohomology Lemma pullback-K-flat and the quasi-isomorphism argument in derived-base-change, after the one-point identification of Tag 0B6A

proof.text: Represent the homotopy objects by cochain complexes using surjectivity of the quotient. The quotient K-flat criterion gives ordinary cochain K-flatness. Apply pointInverseEvaluation_isKFlat to obtain sheaf IsKFlatness of the inverse-evaluated complex.

Use h degreewise as eqToIso to identify P applied termwise with concrete tensorPullbackComplex of the inverse-evaluated complex. The formula hm proves compatibility with every differential. Apply isKFlat_pullback and transport acyclic tensors through the resulting complex isomorphism. Convert sheaf IsKFlatness back to generic K-flatness using kFlat_iff_preserves_acyclic and the tensor braiding, and then pass to the homotopy quotient.

For the morphism assertion lift the homotopy map to a cochain map using quotient fullness. Inverse evaluation is an exact equivalence, so preserves this quasi-isomorphism. Apply exact module inverse image. Its K-flat preservation follows from isKFlat_pullback with the adjunction-unit structure map, transported by exists_inverseImage_tensorPullback_iso. Construct the actual change-of-rings functor sectionwise and sheafify; apply changeOfRings_kFlat_quasiIso. The equalities h and hm form a natural isomorphism from the three-fold composite to P, so transport the quasi-isomorphism to P and use the quotient criterion and localization inversion.
